researchPlan.outcomeQuestion: Did trilateral missile-warning information sharing operate on an ongoing basis after the Camp David commitments?
researchPlan.baselineRequirement: Document pre-August-2023 information-sharing arrangements and operational limits.
researchPlan.followupRequirement: Find dated US/Japan/ROK defense ministry reports of operational exchanges, exercises, and continuity.
researchPlan.attributionAlternatives: Pre-existing US bilateral alliances and independent Japan-ROK reconciliation.
researchPlan.costRequirement: Identify direct defense coordination costs and concessions in comparable units.

observedEvidence.finding: August 18, 2023: US, Japan and South Korea committed to activate trilateral real-time DPRK missile-warning data sharing. November 2023: ministers reported final-stage testing. December 19, 2023: all three governments announced full activation following operational tests. This is a documented change from prior separate US bilateral data-sharing arrangements, not proof of unilateral US influence.

baseline.description: United States shared DPRK missile-warning information separately with Japan and South Korea; the new trilateral real-time mechanism had not yet been fully activated.

followup.description: Trilateral real-time missile-warning mechanism fully activated according to US and Japanese defense ministries.

observedEvidence.caveat: Official ministry statements corroborate activation but are not independent operational performance data. Shared Japanese and Korean agency, duration of operation, costs and counterfactual remain unresolved.

measurementQuality.reason: Qualitative pre/post operational activation documented by multiple governments, but not a matched quantitative outcome series or independently validated operational performance.

sourceAudit.notes: US and Japanese defense ministry releases and US Pacific Command statements located and reviewed for dated operational activation claim. Full independent claim-level audit (reviewer, publication-date check, definition reconciliation) remains pending. Source-anchor reconciliation: Anchor December 2023 operational activation claim to dated trilateral defense joint statement rather than August Camp David announcement; source still requires claim-level independent audit.

externalSourceCrossCheck.claim: US-Japan-ROK trilateral real-time DPRK missile-warning data sharing was activated on 19 December 2023.
externalSourceCrossCheck.limitations: Operational activation is reported, not independently measured performance or US-exclusive causation.

researchPlan.outcomeQuestion: Were Saudi and Iranian diplomatic missions reopened and relations maintained after the Beijing statement?
researchPlan.baselineRequirement: Document diplomatic representation and negotiation milestones before March 2023.
researchPlan.followupRequirement: Find dated embassy reopening records and subsequent bilateral meetings from Saudi and Iranian foreign ministries.
researchPlan.attributionAlternatives: Earlier Iraqi/Omani mediation and Saudi-Iranian strategic interests.
researchPlan.costRequirement: Identify concessions, security outcomes and any costs attributable to mediation.

observedEvidence.finding: Saudi Arabia and Iran agreed in Beijing on 10 March 2023 to resume diplomatic ties and reopen missions within two months. Iran reopened its embassy in Riyadh in June 2023; Saudi Arabia's embassy in Tehran resumed operations in August 2023. The embassy reopening milestones occurred after the agreement, but beyond its initial two-month target.

baseline.description: Diplomatic ties severed in 2016; Iraqi and Omani talks occurred during 2021–2022.

followup.description: Iranian and Saudi embassies reopened in their counterpart capitals.

observedEvidence.caveat: Diplomatic representation resumed, but independent quantitative influence, exclusive Chinese attribution, long-term durability and net costs remain unresolved. Earlier Iraq/Oman mediation was explicitly acknowledged.

measurementQuality.reason: Diplomatic mission reopening documented by contemporary reporting and CRS review; no matched quantitative influence metric or causal counterfactual.

sourceAudit.notes: Source citation recorded in prior milestone; independent claim-by-claim verification not yet recorded. Source-anchor reconciliation: Corrected stale US-GCC statement as unrelated to Saudi-Iran diplomatic restoration; primary source is Saudi Press Agency Beijing joint statement.

externalSourceCrossCheck.claim: Saudi and Iranian embassies reopened after the March 2023 Beijing agreement: Iran in Riyadh in June, Saudi Arabia in Tehran by August.
externalSourceCrossCheck.limitations: Embassy operations reported by news agencies citing government statements; earlier Iraqi/Omani mediation prevents exclusive attribution to China.

researchPlan.outcomeQuestion: Did Belarus alter security posture or operational cooperation following treaty entry into force?
researchPlan.baselineRequirement: Document pre-March-2025 Belarus-Russia military integration and commitments.
researchPlan.followupRequirement: Find dated Belarusian government implementation orders and independently corroborated operational changes.
researchPlan.attributionAlternatives: Pre-existing Union State obligations and Belarus's own security choices.
researchPlan.costRequirement: Identify financing, sovereignty concessions, and sanctions-related consequences.

observedEvidence.finding: Treaty signed 6 December 2024, ratified by Russia in February 2025 and entered into force 13 March 2025. Prior to signature, Belarus had already supported Russia's 2022 invasion, hosted Russian forces and missile systems, and engaged in Union State security cooperation. The treaty codifies security commitments; it does not establish that these earlier behaviors resulted from the treaty.

baseline.description: Belarus hosted Russian troops during 2022 invasion preparations and permitted strikes from its territory; Russian missile deployments and joint defense cooperation predated December 2024 treaty.

followup.description: Security guarantees treaty legally entered into force after exchange of ratification instruments; no independently matched incremental operational outcome is established.

observedEvidence.caveat: Preexisting Russian military access is a confounder, not an attributable post-treaty outcome. Treaty entry into force is a legal milestone, not independent evidence of behavioral implementation or net influence.

measurementQuality.reason: Pre-treaty military integration is documented and legal entry into force independently corroborated, but no measured incremental Belarusian behavior after March 2025 is established.

sourceAudit.notes: Cross-checked treaty date against published treaty, Interfax, CRS and European Parliament background. Claim-level audit remains pending because an independently measured behavioral outcome and reviewer sign-off are absent. Source-anchor reconciliation: Russian treaty publication supports legal milestone only, not post-treaty military behavior.

outcomeAttributionAudit.claim: Treaty entry into force is a legal milestone; prior Belarus-Russia security integration cannot be counted as a treaty-induced outcome.
outcomeAttributionAudit.baselineConfounder: Russian access to Belarusian territory and joint military activities existed before December 2024.
outcomeAttributionAudit.nextVerification: Locate a dated post-13-March-2025 Belarusian policy or operational change with pre-treaty comparator and independent corroboration.

researchPlan.outcomeQuestion: Did Moldova implement new security measures attributable to the May 2024 EU partnership?
researchPlan.baselineRequirement: Document Moldova-EU cooperation and assistance already underway before May 2024.
researchPlan.followupRequirement: Find Moldovan government implementation decisions and EU mission delivery reports with dates and measurable outputs.

observedEvidence.finding: EU–Moldova Security and Defence Partnership signed May 2024. Moldova's foreign ministry confirmed in May 2025 that EUPM assistance included contributions to a crisis-management center concept, cybersecurity agency assistance and equipment; mission began in May 2023. A November 2025 joint dialogue recommitted to cybersecurity and hybrid-threat cooperation. These are operational cooperation observations, not demonstrated incremental outcomes caused by the 2024 partnership.

baseline.description: EU Partnership Mission active before 2024 partnership; Moldovan cyber institutions launched February 2024.

followup.description: Moldovan ministry described specific technical assistance and the parties renewed cooperation commitments.

observedEvidence.caveat: Pre-existing EUPM and EU funding mean program outputs cannot be attributed to the May 2024 partnership without project-specific baseline, timeline, counterpart action and counterfactual.

measurementQuality.reason: Dated mission baseline and subsequent cooperation described, but not a matched outcome attributable to the partnership.

sourceAudit.notes: Source citation recorded in prior milestone; independent claim-by-claim verification not yet recorded. Source-anchor reconciliation: Corrected source anchor from earlier EUPM mission background to actual EU–Moldova Security and Defence Partnership announcement; earlier EUPM source retained as baseline context.

outcomeAttributionAudit.baselineConfounder: EU Partnership Mission and Moldovan cyber institution-building predate the partnership.
outcomeAttributionAudit.nextVerification: Match specific post-partnership Moldovan implementation outputs to dated commitments and separate pre-existing mission deliverables.

researchPlan.outcomeQuestion: Did CEPA change eligible product trade volumes or tariff use compared with a defensible pre-2022 baseline?
researchPlan.baselineRequirement: Collect matched pre-CEPA product-level trade, tariff, and demand data.
researchPlan.followupRequirement: Collect comparable customs tariff utilization and trade quantities for 2022 onward.
researchPlan.attributionAlternatives: Energy prices, global trade rebound, exchange rates and UAE demand.
researchPlan.costRequirement: Measure tariff revenue forgone, adjustment costs and bilateral distributional effects.

observedEvidence.caveat: Indian fiscal-year figures; FY2020-21 was pandemic-affected, and trade prices/volumes and broader recovery confound attribution. This is nominal gross trade, not net benefit. FY2021-22 pre-agreement trade was already USD 72.9 billion, showing substantial recovery before CEPA entered into force; avoid treating FY2020-21 as a representative unaffected baseline.

preAgreementContext.note: This fiscal year preceded CEPA entry into force on May 1, 2022; nominal bilateral trade had already recovered sharply from pandemic-era FY2020-21.

measurementQuality.reason: Aggregate nominal merchandise trade in matching units is observed, but pre-period pandemic distortion, composition and price effects, counterfactual and independent outcome validation remain unresolved.

sourceAudit.notes: Source citation recorded in prior milestone; independent claim-by-claim verification not yet recorded. Source-anchor reconciliation: India nominal trade series is government-reported and descriptive, not an independent causal estimate.

outcomeAttributionAudit.claim: India-UAE merchandise trade comparison is descriptive, and the pandemic-affected FY2020-21 baseline exaggerates apparent post-agreement growth.
outcomeAttributionAudit.baselineConfounder: Pre-CEPA FY2021-22 nominal trade had already recovered to USD 72.9 billion from USD 43.3 billion in FY2020-21.
outcomeAttributionAudit.nextVerification: Obtain tariff-line or product-level pre/post CEPA utilization and quantities; separate price and energy effects from policy effects.

evidenceAuditMethodology: Source-identified event records are not independently verified causal influence. Gate statuses indicate research coverage, not outcomes or influence. Empty gate means unassessed, not zero. Each sphere is reviewed against the same six gates.
researchPlanMethodology: Pre-registered research questions and source categories. Planned research is not a completed evidence audit. Never promote planned outcomes into measurements.
observationPolicy: Documented observation is not attributable influence. Only matched periods/definitions may support before-after differences; no cross-case ranking. Context from earlier initiatives must be disclosed.
measurementQualityPolicy: Measurement readiness is separate from research activity, source identification, and diplomatic influence. The five checks must all pass before a candidate can be called a comparable outcome measurement; even then causal attribution is a separate gate.
sourceAuditPolicy: No URL is marked independently verified merely because it is listed. Source access, exact claim, publication date, matched definitions and reviewer must be recorded. Missing audit remains pending; no inferred influence.
